question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>λ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Consider the system of linear equations <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>λ</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Which of the following statement is INCORRECT?

options.text: If <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo></math> then the system has infinitely many solutions for all values of <math><mi>λ</mi></math> and <math><mi>μ</mi></math>
If <math><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo></math> then the system has a unique solution for all values of <math><mi>λ</mi></math> and <math><mi>μ</mi></math>
If <math><mi>λ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></math> then the system has infinitely many solutions for <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>
If <math><mi>λ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></math> then the system has no solution for <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>

solution.text:
ax+2y=λ
3x-2y=μ
For a=-3, above lines will be parallel or coincident
Also parallel for λ+μ≠0 and coincident λ+μ=0
and if a≠-3, lines are intersecting ⇒ unique solution.
